datasets.title: Satellite detected waters extents, as of 16 August 2019 over Khartoum, EI Gazira and White Nile State, Sudan
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20190815SDN This map illustrates satellite-detected surface water in Khartoum, EI Gazira and White Nile State, Sudan as observed from Sentinel-2 imagery acquired on 16 August 2019. Within the analysed extent of about 41,600 sq km, a total about 2,061 sq km of lands appear to be flooded as of 16 August 2019. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR - UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/waters-extents-as-of-16-august-2019-over-khartoum-ei-gazira-and-white-nile-state-sudan]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts interpreted Sentinel-2 satellite imagery acquired on 16 August 2019 over a 41,600 sq km extent in Sudan, identifying and delineating surface water through visual comparison and change detection analysis. The resulting water extent polygons with area measurements represent observed flood hazard at a single point in time, preliminary and unvalidated in the field.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Sentinel-2 satellite imagery analysis providing observed surface water extent mapping through visual interpretation and change detection between satellite images
